section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Creativity & Thinking (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A student who generates many different, original, and unusual uses for a common object like a brick (building material, paperweight, doorstop, weapon, art piece) is demonstrating which type of thinking, considered the hallmark of creativity?
explanation: Divergent thinking generates many varied, original possibilities from a single starting point — the opposite of convergent thinking, which narrows toward one correct answer.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Creativity & Thinking (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Graham Wallas described the creative process as occurring in four stages: gathering information and defining the problem; setting the problem aside while the mind works on it unconsciously; a sudden 'Aha!' moment of insight; and finally testing and refining the idea. These four stages are respectively called:
explanation: Wallas's four-stage model of the creative process is Preparation, Incubation, Illumination, and Verification — a classic, frequently-tested creativity model.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Creativity & Thinking (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A widely-used standardised test that measures a person's creativity by assessing fluency (number of ideas), flexibility (variety of ideas), originality (uniqueness of ideas), and elaboration (detail added to ideas) is the:
explanation: The Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking measure fluency, flexibility, originality, and elaboration — the four key components of creative ability.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Creativity & Thinking (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Which classroom practice is LEAST likely to nurture creativity in students?

options.option_text: Insisting on one single 'correct' method for every task and penalising any deviation
Encouraging students to ask unusual questions and explore multiple solutions
Providing open-ended tasks with no single fixed answer
Rewarding original ideas rather than only accuracy

explanation: Rigid insistence on a single correct method and penalising deviation suppresses divergent thinking and risk-taking, both essential to creativity.
